Q1: Ammonium nitrate is recognized by official GHS standards (Tier 1) for organ and systemic hazards. It also shows potential hazards in environmental, endocrine disruption, inhalation, oral, and dermal/eye categories based on an expanded scientific perspective (Tier 2). Data for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and reproductive hazards are currently insufficient for a confident assessment (Tier 4).
Q2: Ammonium nitrate is listed on the TEDX (The Endocrine Disruption Exchange) list as a potential endocrine disruptor, indicating scientific evidence for this concern. It is not currently found on any lists designating chemicals of low hazard.
Q3: Ammonium nitrate is extensively characterized, evidenced by 51,000 scientific literature references in the SciFinder database, significantly higher than the median for our dataset of petrochemical materials. Its well-defined molecular formula (H3N.HNO3) and substance class, along with it not being a UVCB, further confirm its detailed characterization. Only its carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, and reproductive hazards profile remains data deficient (Tier 4).
